blocks.title: Dividing the work
blocks.md: In **division of labour**, making a product is split into stages and each worker does one stage. In a shirt workshop one person cuts, another sews and a third irons. **Specialisation** means a person, a firm or a region concentrates on one thing it does well. Specialising means people make more than they need of one good, so they must **exchange** the extra for other goods.

blocks.title: Advantages and disadvantages
blocks.md: **Advantages**: workers become skilled and fast; time is saved; output rises; goods may become cheaper. **Disadvantages**: the work can be boring and repetitive; workers may not learn other skills; if one stage stops, the whole process stops; people depend on others for the goods they do not make.

items.text: Division of labour in a tailoring shop

blocks.caption: Division of labour in a tailoring shop: three workers, three tasks.
blocks.alt: A three-row table showing the cutter, the sewer and the person who irons and packs.

blocks.title: Why exchange matters
blocks.md: A farmer in the West may specialise in maize and a fisherman in Limbe in fish. Each needs what the other produces, so they trade, using **money** to make exchange easy. The bigger the market, the more specialisation is possible. Good roads and markets help exchange.

blocks.title: Do not mix
blocks.md: **Division of labour** is about **tasks inside** one production process; **specialisation** is wider and may concern whole regions or countries. Not all work can be divided: a single artist painting a picture cannot easily divide tasks. Too much division can make work dull.

blocks.title: Worked example — more output
blocks.statement: Twelve tailors each make 4 shirts a week working alone. When tasks are divided, the group makes 72 shirts a week (illustrative). Find output per tailor before and after.
steps: Output per worker has risen by 2 shirts.

blocks.title: Worked example — why exchange
blocks.statement: A farmer in Bali grows only maize. She needs salt, soap and school books. How does she get them?
steps: She keeps some maize for her family.
She sells the extra maize at the market for money.
She uses the money to buy the salt, soap and books.
blocks.answer: By selling her surplus and using the money
